argument_summary: The present record does not support the broad claim that a 4% reversible rollout and monitoring alone satisfy policy for an exposed material weakness. It does support a narrower certification posture: aggregate readiness cleared by 2.2 points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, staged rollout, rollback capability, and public governance guidance can justify launch readiness overall, while the exposed enterprise refund workflow limitation must be treated as an explicit disclosed limitation rather than as a resolved issue. The audit concern is therefore overstated to the extent it treats the packet as claiming rollout controls eliminate the disclosure obligation; the stronger reading is that certification is defensible only as a limited, disclosed case.
claims_about_policy: The policy text cuts against any argument that rollback, dashboards, or a small initial percentage substitute for disclosure when the affected segment remains exposed. The admissible evidence also shows the affected enterprise refund workflow is still eligible in the initial cohort and that the available risk-acceptance draft is not approved and does not name that exposure. On this record, the supportable policy position is not 'controls are sufficient by themselves'; it is that certification can proceed only as a caveated case in which the known limitation remains disclosed in the certification posture. That narrows the claim to fit the admissible evidence rather than asserting clean compliance on rollout controls alone.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not necessary if the auditor can record this as a caveated certification posture rather than a clean controls-based compliance finding. That preserves governance fidelity without requiring the packet to overclaim what the current evidence proves.
concessions: The affected enterprise refund workflow remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The random workspace gate does not exclude the affected use case.
The available risk-acceptance draft is not approved and does not specifically cover the exposed refund workflow.
The current record does not support treating rollout reversibility and monitoring as a substitute for disclosure.
